checks.name: Diagnosis identifies the exclusive upper bound and a concrete equality/empty counterexample
Real source context was read through a successful completed tool receipt

output.summary: Diagnosed the failing contract in src/bounds.ts. inBounds uses `index <= length` instead of `index < length`, an off-by-one that accepts index == length and accepts index 0 for empty collections (length 0), violating the contract that valid indices are 0 through length-1 and empty collections have no valid index.

findings.title: inBounds accepts out-of-range indices due to off-by-one upper bound
findings.body: The predicate returns `index >= 0 && index <= length`. The contract requires valid indices to be 0 through length-1, so the upper comparison must be strict (`index < length`). Using `<=` makes index == length pass and makes every nonnegative index pass when length == 0.
findings.evidence: inBounds(3,3) evaluates (3>=0 && 3<=3) = true, but valid indices for length 3 are 0,1,2 so expected false (frozen counterexample). inBounds(0,0) evaluates (0>=0 && 0<=0) = true, but an empty collection has no valid index so expected false (frozen counterexample).
findings.suggestion: Change the return expression to `index >= 0 && index < length` so the upper bound is exclusive, preserving the public function contract.

output.diagnosis: Off-by-one in the upper-bound comparison: `index <= length` should be `index < length`, causing index == length and all nonnegative indices for length == 0 to be incorrectly reported as in-bounds.
